builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs
summary: DUALQUANT replaces calibration-data-dependent activation quantization (e.g., SmoothQuant) and weight-only quantization with a calibration-free dual-scale method derived from weight-reconstruction MSE minimization, supporting MX and NVFP4 block formats. It costs the engineering effort of integrating a packed W4A4 kernel path and incurs some accuracy degradation relative to BF16, though the reported solver has closed-form updates and no calibration pipeline to maintain. It can fail on workloads whose accuracy tolerance is tighter than WikiText-2/C4 zero-shot benchmarks suggest, on models outside the evaluated Llama/Qwen families, and where native 4-bit hardware or mature W4A4 kernels are unavailable.
rationale: The method runs on the reader's exact hardware class (single 24 GB GPU) with a validated real-kernel speedup and no calibration data requirement, but W4A4 activation quantization quality is workload-sensitive and should be validated on the reader's own tasks before production adoption.

claims.statement: DUALQUANT replaces calibration-data-dependent activation quantization (e.g., SmoothQuant) and weight-only quantization with a calibration-free dual-scale method derived from weight-reconstruction MSE minimization, supporting MX and NVFP4 block formats. It costs the engineering effort of integrating a packed W4A4 kernel path and incurs some accuracy degradation relative to BF16, though the reported solver has closed-form updates and no calibration pipeline to maintain. It can fail on workloads whose accuracy tolerance is tighter than WikiText-2/C4 zero-shot benchmarks suggest, on models outside the evaluated Llama/Qwen families, and where native 4-bit hardware or mature W4A4 kernels are unavailable.
Up to 2.46x throughput speedup and 2.61x memory reduction over BF16 on a real packed W4A4 Llama-3.1-8B path on an RTX 4090, with accuracy matching or exceeding calibration-based SmoothQuant.
